name: Duplicate QT8.1 — Duplicate of Open Claim (Process Earlier & Reject) Navigator
description: Resolve the PX_DP1/PX_QT8 hard edits flagging a duplicate of an open (still-pending) claim: confirm the LOB via Product, identify the electronic receipt method from the DCN camera reel, rule out corrected-claim events, compare the duplicate claim, review the history claim, confirm an exact field match and an Open (Pending-Investigation) status, apply FIFO by comparing the receipt dates, then reject the later current claim with code PX_RDUP00.

steps.name: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT8 hard edits
steps.description: The app will display all edits in the Event Resolution tab, with the PX_DP1 and PX_QT8 hard edits highlighted with an error indication — these are the current events to resolve. PX_QT8 indicates a duplicate of an open claim, meaning the original (history) claim is still pending and not finalized. The action under PX_QT8 is to process the earlier claim first (FIFO) and then reject the later claim as a duplicate.
steps.hint: Open the 'Event Resolution' tab. The PX_DP1 and PX_QT8 edits are active and highlighted in red.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes as soon as the trainee opens the Event Resolution tab.
steps.checklistItem: Identify the PX_DP1 and PX_QT8 hard edits

steps.name: Check the Line of Business via Product field
steps.description: Determine whether the claim is ITS or another Line of Business (LOB) by navigating to the Member Information tab, then the Group Information section, and reviewing the Product field. For ITS claims, the Product field may display values such as Local, National, or ACA. If the Product value is not Local, follow the alternate guidelines. If the Product value is Local, proceed to the next step. In this scenario, the Product is Local; therefore, the trainee may proceed. Also determine whether the claim was received electronically (alphanumeric) or by paper (numeric) by inspecting the DCN number
steps.hint: Open 'Member Info' and read the Product field under the Group section — it reads 'Local'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the Member Info tab to read the Product field.
steps.checklistItem: Check the Line of Business via Product field

steps.name: Check for corrected claim events (PX_PAJ/PX_SCB)
steps.description: Determine whether the claim contains corrected claim events by looking for PX_PAJ or PX_SCB events in the Event Resolution tab. If corrected claim events are present, follow the corrected events guidelines; if absent, proceed. In this scenario, the claim does not contain corrected claim events, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Return to 'Event Resolution' and scan the All Edits list — there are no PX_PAJ or PX_SCB corrected-claim events.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee revisits the Event Resolution tab to rule out corrected-claim events.

steps.name: Trigger the duplicate-claim comparison
steps.description: Obtain the potential duplicate claim(s) by navigating to the Claim Data tab, then the Duplicate sub-tab. Review the list of potential duplicate claims displayed in the table. Select the applicable duplicate claim using the radio button in the first column, then click Compare Claim. Once the comparison is initiated, a new section titled Claim Compare Results will appear below the duplicates table. Within this section, review the Show Differences subsection to identify and evaluate any differences between the current claim and the selected potential duplicate claim.
steps.hint: Open Claim Data → Duplicate, select the duplicate line's radio, then click 'Compare Claim'.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee selects the duplicate radio and clicks Compare Claim (dispatches the compare_claim action).

steps.name: Confirm the claim is a duplicate
steps.description: Review the Claim compare results to determine whether the claim is a true duplicate by checking the following fields under the Show differences section: Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering provider or license number under Provider information section and Attachments under attachments tab. If none of these fields are listed in the Claim compare results, it means the current claim and the history claim are the same — no differences exist, confirming a duplicate. In this scenario, the claim is a duplicate; all accordions (Attachments, Additional claim data, Provider, Claim header, Claim lines) are shown but contain no differing data.
steps.hint: Expand the Claim Compare Results accordions — they show no differing data, confirming a true duplicate.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee reviews the compare-results accordions (dispatches review_duplicate).
steps.checklistItem: Confirm the claim is a duplicate

steps.name: Verify the history claim was processed correctly
steps.description: Determine whether the history (duplicate) claim was processed correctly. Click the Open claim detail button to open the history claim. The system displays a message: "In real application, you need to follow guidelines to check if the history claim is processed correctly. In this scenario, consider this history claim is processed correctly." The pop-up also shows the history claim's receipt date (4/6/2026), needed later for the FIFO comparison. If the history claim was processed incorrectly, it must be adjusted and processed correctly before proceeding; if it was processed correctly, proceed. In this scenario, the history claim is processed correctly, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Click 'Open Claim Detail' on the history claim, read the advisory message and note the receipt date (4/6/2026), then proceed.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee opens the history claim detail pop-up (dispatches open_claim_detail).
steps.checklistItem: Verify the history claim was processed correctly

steps.name: Confirm all claim fields match the history claim
steps.description: Compare claim information between the current claim and the history claim to confirm an exact match across all relevant fields: Tax ID, Group or Provider name, Rendering provider or license number, Attachments, Date of service, Place of treatment, Procedure code, Modifiers, Diagnosis codes, National Drug Codes, Billed amount, and Units of occurrence. These values need to be noted from both the current claim and the history claim for comparison. For now, click the Confirm match button — the values of these fields from both claims will be listed for review. If any field does not match, follow the alternate guidelines; if all fields match, proceed. In this scenario, all information matches, so the trainee proceeds.
steps.hint: Open the Matching Duplicate Information panel — every field matches the history claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee confirms the matching-field list (dispatches review_matching).
steps.checklistItem: Confirm all claim fields match the history claim

steps.name: Verify history claim is Open (Pending-Investigation)
steps.description: Validate whether the history claim is finalized or open by checking the status field on the claim summary of the history claim (the status is also visible in the rightmost column of the claims listing table). For now, click the Check related status button — the status of the history claim will be displayed. If the status is Pending-Investigation, the claim is open; if the status is Resolved, the claim is finalized and Paid. In this scenario, the history claim status is Open (Pending-Investigation), so the trainee proceeds to compare receipt dates and apply FIFO.
steps.hint: Check the related claim status — it reads 'Open (Pending-Investigation)', so the history claim is still open and not finalized.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee checks the related claim status (dispatches review_related_status).

steps.name: Apply FIFO by comparing receipt dates
steps.description: Apply the FIFO rule: compare the Receipt dates on both the current claim and the history claim, process the earliest (first in) claim per the standard guidelines and contract benefits, and reject the later (second in) claim as a duplicate. For now, click the Compare receipt dates button — the receipt dates of both claims will be displayed. If the current claim's receipt date is earlier, process the current claim and reject the history claim. If the history claim's receipt date is earlier, the history claim came in first — reject the current claim as a duplicate. In this scenario, the history claim was received on 4/6/2026 and the current claim was received on 5/11/2026. The history claim came in first, so the current claim is the later submission and must be rejected as a duplicate.
steps.hint: Click 'Compare receipt dates' — the history claim (4/6/2026) is earlier than the current claim (5/11/2026), so reject the current claim.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee compares the receipt dates and applies FIFO (dispatches review_receipt_dates).
steps.checklistItem: Apply FIFO by comparing receipt dates

steps.name: Reject the duplicate claim with code PX_RDUP00
steps.description: Reject the current claim as a duplicate. Navigate to the Action menu and select Deny claim. Enter the rejection code "PX_RDUP00" in the rejection code field, then click Submit in the Reject panel.
steps.hint: Action menu → Deny claim. Enter reject code PX_RDUP00 and click Submit in the Reject panel.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Reject (Deny) panel with code PX_RDUP00 (dispatches the deny_claim action).
steps.checklistItem: Reject the duplicate claim with code PX_RDUP00

steps.name: Submit the Reject decision
steps.description: After confirming the Reject panel, click the Submit button to finalize the Reject decision and complete the attempt.
steps.hint: Click the Submit button to finalize the Reject decision.
steps.completionTriggerNote: Completes when the trainee submits the Reject (Deny) decision with the Submit button.

stepSummaryForResults.name: All fields matched the history claim
FIFO applied — current claim is the later submission
